word-counter.what: Counts the words in your text instantly, including how it treats contractions, hyphenated words and apostrophes.
word-counter.howto: Paste or type your text into the box. The word and character counts update live, so you can trim to a target length as you write. Use it to hit a publication's word limit, a blog post length, or a word-count goal for a session.
word-counter.why: Word count is one of the few concrete, enforceable limits in writing. Editors and guidelines state a range; a word counter lets you meet it exactly instead of counting manually.

character-counter.what: Counts the characters in your text, counting spaces.
character-counter.howto: Paste your text to see the total character count immediately. This is the number platforms use for tweet lengths, meta descriptions, SMS and other strict limits.
character-counter.why: Character limits are everywhere — social posts, form fields, headlines. Knowing your count before you paste saves you from truncation.

character-counter-no-spaces.what: Counts the characters in your text excluding spaces.
character-counter-no-spaces.howto: Paste text to see the character count with spaces removed. Useful for limits that exclude whitespace, and for comparing how much actual content you have.
character-counter-no-spaces.why: Some application forms and database fields count only non-space characters, so knowing both numbers is useful.

sentence-counter.what: Counts sentences and paragraphs in your text.
sentence-counter.howto: Paste your text to get both a sentence count and a paragraph count. Use the sentence count with the sentence-length checker to see the average length.
sentence-counter.why: Sentence and paragraph counts reveal the rhythm and readability of a piece. A wall of very long sentences is harder to read.

paragraph-counter.what: Counts the paragraphs in your text.
paragraph-counter.howto: Paste your text and the paragraph count appears instantly. A paragraph is normally split by a blank line.
paragraph-counter.why: Paragraphs are a visual signal of readability. Short paragraphs read faster online; knowing your count helps you balance them.

reading-time.what: Estimates how long it takes to read your text aloud at an average pace.
reading-time.howto: Paste or write your text and see the estimated reading time. Use it to match a newsletter, speech or article to the time a reader or listener will give it.
reading-time.why: Reading time sets expectations. A reader decides in seconds whether to commit, and a clear estimate respects their time.

word-density.what: Finds the most frequent words in your text and shows how often each appears.
word-density.howto: Paste your text to see a ranked list of your most-used words and their repetition rates. Spot a filler word you lean on and replace it.
word-density.why: Repetitive words weaken writing. Seeing your patterns is the fastest way to notice crutch words and overused phrases.

case-converter.what: Converts text between title case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, sentence case and camelCase.
case-converter.howto: Type or paste text, pick the case you need, and copy the result. Title case is for headings; sentence case for normal sentences.
case-converter.why: Case rules differ by context — a headline, a code comment, a database entry. Converting in one click avoids retyping.

text-cleaner.what: Removes double spaces, stray line breaks and other messy formatting from pasted text.
text-cleaner.howto: Paste messy text and get clean, consistent text back with normal spaces and breaks. Useful when you copy from an email, a PDF or a website.
text-cleaner.why: Copied text is rarely clean. A cleaner saves you from manually fixing spacing and line breaks before you submit or publish.

remove-extra-spaces.what: Turns runs of spaces into single spaces.
remove-extra-spaces.howto: Paste text to collapse extra spaces into normal spacing. Ideal for cleaning text pasted from formatted sources.
remove-extra-spaces.why: Double spaces and irregular gaps make a document look sloppy. One pass cleans the whole thing.

line-break-cleaner.what: Fixes inconsistent line breaks in pasted text.
line-break-cleaner.howto: Paste text with stray or missing line breaks and get a clean result. Great for text pasted from PDFs or web pages.
line-break-cleaner.why: Pasted text often inherits odd breaks. Cleaning them makes a document reliable before editing.

text-sorter.what: Sorts lines of text alphabetically, ascending or descending.
text-sorter.howto: Paste a list and choose A-Z or Z-A. Useful for organising headings, a bibliography or a list of items.
text-sorter.why: Alphabetical order is a common requirement in references and lists. Sorting by hand is tedious and error-prone.

duplicate-line-remover.what: Removes repeated lines from a list, keeping one of each.
duplicate-line-remover.howto: Paste a list with duplicates and get a clean, deduplicated version. Useful for cleaning data or a long list.
duplicate-line-remover.why: Removing duplicates makes a list reliable and easier to read, whatever you are compiling.

writing-timer.what: A focus timer for a writing session.
writing-timer.howto: Set a goal in minutes, then write without stopping. The timer keeps you honest without nagging, and many writers find a fixed block easier than an open-ended session.
writing-timer.why: A timer turns 'be good' into 'fill the time' — making it far easier to start and to keep a routine.

article-outline-generator.what: Turns an idea into a structured article outline with an introduction, body sections and a conclusion.
article-outline-generator.howto: Enter your topic and the tool builds a skeleton you can rewrite into a full draft. Adjust sections to your argument and fill them in.
article-outline-generator.why: An outline removes the hardest part of starting. A clear structure means each paragraph has a job, so you write faster.

writing-checklist-generator.what: Generates a pre-publication checklist for your writing.
writing-checklist-generator.howto: Select the checks that apply and work through them before you publish or submit.
writing-checklist-generator.why: A checklist catches the easy, costly mistakes — typos, weak conclusions, missing citations — before an editor does.

syllable-counter.what: Counts the syllables in words and text.
syllable-counter.howto: Paste text to count syllables. Useful for poetry, songwriting and assessing rhythm.
syllable-counter.why: Syllables govern rhythm in poetry and verse. A syllable count helps you match a metre or a line length.

readability-score.what: Scores how easy your text is to read using established readability formulas.
readability-score.howto: Paste your text and see readability scores such as the Flesch reading ease and grade level. Aim for clear, accessible writing for a general reader.
readability-score.why: Readability is not about dumbing down — it is about clarity. A high score means your reader can follow you on the first pass.

filler-word-finder.what: Finds filler words and hedges like 'very', 'really' and 'in my opinion'.
filler-word-finder.howto: Paste your text to spot filler words and cut the ones that add nothing. Removing them makes the writing sharper.
filler-word-finder.why: Filler and hedge words dilute an argument. Cutting them is one of the fastest edits for stronger prose.

passive-voice-detector.what: Flags sentences that may be in the passive voice.
passive-voice-detector.howto: Paste text to find candidate passive constructions. Review each and rewrite to active where the doer matters.
passive-voice-detector.why: Active voice is usually clearer and more direct. Identifying passive spots is quicker than hunting for them manually.

word-repetition-checker.what: Finds words repeated too close together across a text.
word-repetition-checker.howto: Paste your text to see where a word repeats. Replace a repeated word with a synonym or restructure the sentence.
word-repetition-checker.why: Repeated words pull a reader's eye and sound mechanical. Varying your vocabulary keeps prose fresh.

sentence-length-checker.what: Identifies sentences that are too long and hard to follow.
sentence-length-checker.howto: Paste text to highlight long sentences. Split them into shorter ones for clarity, or give a favourite long one a brief break.
sentence-length-checker.why: Long, unbroken sentences lose readers. Marking them is the first step to a clearer rhythm.

cliche-detector.what: Finds overused cliches and stock phrases.
cliche-detector.howto: Paste text to spot cliches and replace them with fresher, more specific language.
cliche-detector.why: Cliches signal a writer is not thinking. Replacing them with specific, original detail is what makes writing memorable.

adverb-finder.what: Finds adverbs, the words that often do the work a stronger verb should.
adverb-finder.howto: Paste text to see where adverbs appear. Consider replacing a weak verb plus adverb ('ran quickly') with one strong verb ('sprinted').
adverb-finder.why: Adverbs can be a sign of a lazy verb. Cutting them often forces sharper, more vivid writing.

title-generator.what: Generates several headline options for your article or post.
title-generator.howto: Enter a topic and get multiple title options. Pick the clearest one or combine the best parts of two.
title-generator.why: Before a reader sees your content, they see your title. A strong, specific headline earns the click.

meta-description-generator.what: Writes a meta description for your page, kept to the length search engines like.
meta-description-generator.howto: Enter your topic and the benefit to the reader, and get a description near the recommended length. Add it to your page's markup.
meta-description-generator.why: A meta description is the snippet shown under a search result. A clear, benefit-led one raises your click-through rate.

random-writing-prompt.what: Gives you a fresh writing prompt to beat the blank page.
random-writing-prompt.howto: Click for a new prompt and write immediately. Don't overthink — the point is to start.
random-writing-prompt.why: Writer's block is often just not knowing where to start. A specific prompt removes that choice and gets you writing.

word-document-converter.what: Turns your text into a Word-compatible document, or plain text.
word-document-converter.howto: Paste or write your text, choose the format, and download. Open it in Word, Google Docs or LibreOffice.
word-document-converter.why: Many submissions and clients want a document file. Creating one in the browser avoids opening a word processor.

pdf-editor.what: Lets you edit a PDF's pages — rotate, delete, reorder — entirely in your browser.
pdf-editor.howto: Open a PDF, then use the controls on each page to rotate, remove or move it. Export a new PDF when you're happy. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-editor.why: A quick fix to a PDF — a rotated scan, a page to drop — shouldn't need uploads or an account. Doing it client-side keeps it private.

pdf-to-text.what: Extracts the text from a PDF so you can copy and reuse it.
pdf-to-text.howto: Choose a PDF and the text is extracted into a box you can copy or edit. Note that scanned/image PDFs may not extract text.
pdf-to-text.why: Sometimes a PDF's words are all you want — to quote, edit, or reuse in your own document.

text-to-pdf.what: Turns plain text into a clean, downloadable PDF.
text-to-pdf.howto: Paste or write text and click to create a PDF. Great for a first draft, a simple report or a shareable version of notes.
text-to-pdf.why: PDFs preserve formatting and are easy to send. Making one from text in the browser is quick and needs no app.

images-to-pdf.what: Combines JPG or PNG images into a single PDF, one image per page.
images-to-pdf.howto: Choose one or more images and the tool builds a PDF with each on its own page.
images-to-pdf.why: Combining scans, screenshots or photos into one shareable PDF is a common task an editor or client may ask for.

self-plagiarism-checker.what: Checks your text for repeated or near-identical sentences within itself.
self-plagiarism-checker.howto: Paste your text to find internal duplication. Review the flagged repeats and vary or remove them.
self-plagiarism-checker.why: Accidental repetition reads as careless. Catching it within a single document is a fast, private quality check.

ai-writing-checker.what: A rule-based look at formulaic phrases and AI-favoured words in your text.
ai-writing-checker.howto: Paste text to get a heuristic AI-likeness score and a list of flagged phrases. Use it to spot a 'flat', generated feel and write more naturally.
ai-writing-checker.why: This is a nudge, not a verdict. No tool can reliably tell human from AI text; it helps you notice a formulaic tone and make it your own.
